title: Autopilot setup answers
description: Answers for `autopilot setup --config <file>`. With --yes, setup runs without prompts and fails on a missing answer it needs. Secret values are never in this file.

backend.description: Where the secrets go. env: files on the host. op: 1Password (vault autopilot). Default: --backend, else env.

app_id.description: ID of an existing GitHub App to use. Without it, setup creates a new App in the browser, which --yes cannot do. With the op backend, its private key must be in 1Password (vault autopilot, document github-app-private-key).

app_key.description: Absolute path of the private key file (.pem) of the App in app_id, for the env backend. Host setup pushes it to a host that has no key. Default: ~/.config/autopilot/app-key.pem, where autopilot app create saves it.

host.description: SSH target of the host (for example user@my-host), or local for this machine. Default: --host or AUTOPILOT_HOST.

owner.description: GitHub login that may start jobs, written to a new host.json. Default: the login of gh.

allow.description: Accounts and owner/repo entries that the host watches.

init.description: Repos (owner/repo) to onboard with autopilot init. Setup skips a repo that already has .github/autopilot.json.

alias.description: Shell alias for autopilot (for example ap), or false for none.
